_README: A LANE PRESET: what a search is looking for and what it is not.
Copied to config/lane-vocab.json by `node setup.mjs`, then yours to edit.
Underscore sections are read by one consumer each (named in `_comment`); every other
top-level key is a shared anti-lane FAMILY that both title scorers read, with one weight
per scorer because each penalty is sized against the bonus it answers.
Patterns in shared families and `_ranker` must be valid in BOTH JavaScript and Python.

_preset.name: general
_preset.description: No field-specific tuning. setup.mjs fills `_ranker`, `_lane` and `_title_filter` from the role keywords you give it.

_ranker._comment: Read by pipeline-audit.mjs --rank. JavaScript regex, case-insensitive. `lanes` add their weight per matching term; `deprioritised` and `managerial` subtract; `out_of_lane` is an outright -99; `ic_director` exempts IC director titles from the managerial penalty.

_lane._comment: Read by scripts/_lane.py (board sweeps). Python regex, case-insensitive.

_assist._comment: Read by scripts/eval-assist.py. Python regex, case-insensitive.
gates: \b(ph\.?d\.?|master'?s degree|ms or phd|advanced degree)\b[^.]{0,60}\b(required|must have|is a requirement)\b|\brequire[sd]?\b[^.]{0,40}\b(ph\.?d\.?|master'?s)\b

_board._comment: Read by the board builders. Each role goes to the FIRST lane whose words appear in ' <lowercased title> '; `cv` is the CV variant the dashboard suggests; lanes with a `button` get a filter button on the boards.

_title_filter._comment: Written into portals.yml title_filter by setup.mjs. Substring match, case-insensitive; at least one positive and no negative must match.

_triage._comment: Read by scripts/triage-leads.py. [label, Python regex]: a pasted lead whose title matches is set aside with that label (still printed, never silently dropped).

_sweep._comment: Read by scripts/nvidia-sweep.py: the search terms it sends to NVIDIA's board. With none, it falls back to the title filter's positives.
